newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine '97 crop forecast revised down.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine '97 crop forecast revised down.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINE 1997 TOTAL GRAIN OUTPUT FORECAST REVISED DOWN

KIEV, June 2 - Our forecast for Ukraine's total grain output this year is revised down to a net 31-33 million tonnes from a previous forecast of 35 million tonnes. But corn (maize) output is likely to rise.
Sunseed output may drop, as a major part of the sunseed area was planted in early May, which is seven to eight days later than the optimal term.
Spring barley output may fall 10-20 percent in the south and 5-10 percent in other regions.
Peas and sugar beet sowings are far below last year's levels. Sowing of sugar beet is going rather slowly, with hot weather causing serious delays.
By mid-May, sowings of spring barley, oats and corn (maize) had exceeded year-ago planting levels.

But hot, dry weather in May, coupled with low soil moisture, has affected the key grain producing regions, particularly in the South, by encouraging producers to plant more corn and less barley and other spring grains.
This is likely to result in a substantial increase in corn output in 1997. By mid-May, corn plantings had already exceeded last year's harvested area by 1.7 times.
